thread:
maria: ping — seeing a ~30% throughput drop across prod-serving-global since 12:34 UTC, lots of worker restarts
jasper: confirmed, graph shows a stair-step drop and then oscillation, tail latency also spiky :grimacing:
kai: I’m on it, digging into node-level logs. any obvious recent deploys?
infra-bot: deploy/redwood-runtime v3.14.0 promoted to prod-serving-global at 11:58 UTC (by release-bot)
anita: not a code rollback yet, but we saw elevated small-batch traffic from a customer run around 12:20 UTC
maria: good call — traffic pattern shifted to many concurrent short sequences, small batches ramped up
jasper: attaching the allocator logs snippet from node gpu-07:
```
[12:34:11] gpu_alloc: slab_free fail, could not satisfy 256MB
[12:34:12] kvcache: evict candidate count=186, scanning
[12:34:12] runtime: kernel_fallback -> selected slow path (cpu memcpy) due to frag
[12:34:13] worker[17]: restarted; exit_code=137 OOM
[12:34:15] allocator: fragment_count=122, largest_free=48MB
```
kai: that matches what I see — repeated evictions and kernel fallback on several GPUs, then oom restarts
anita: I ran a quick profile with profiling-bot on the 12:30-12:40 window, summary below:
profiling-bot: CPU usage up for manager process during kv eviction, GPU used memory fragmenting, average batch size fell from 8->2
profiling-bot: hot paths:
- kvcache::evict_scan (40%)
- kernel_selector::choose (20%) -> fallback to memcpy slow path when contiguous block < required
- request_coordinator::dispatch (15%)
jasper: so small batches + KV eviction churn -> fragmentation -> kernel fallback -> increased memory pressure -> OOM -> worker restarts -> throughput drop loop
maria: are we seeing noisy-tenant on these nodes? any single tenant sending many tiny requests?
kai: yes, the tenant id x-tenant-94 has a spike, 90% of short sequences over the last 5m
anita: mitigation idea: temporarily increase per-tenant rate limit for small requests? or better: enable aggressive prefix cache pinning for popular keys to reduce eviction frequency
jasper: quick mitigation I can push: 1) disable fallback to the slow memcpy kernel for 10m to avoid additional fragmentation (will make some requests error instead of thrashing) 2) raise kvcache max_evict_scan_ms to slow down churn
sre-oncall: prefer non-destructive first — can we throttle the noisy tenant instead of kernel toggles?
maria: agree, throttle first. jasper, can you apply a targeted throttle for x-tenant-94 and set alert to auto-unfreeze after 15m?
jasper: doing it now — applying token bucket throttle 100 req/s for x-tenant-94
infra-bot: rate-limit rule applied to x-tenant-94 (100r/s) by jasper at 12:41:22 UTC
kai: after throttle the eviction rate dropped and largest_free increased from ~48MB->~128MB over 3m, no new worker restarts observed
anita: perf numbers post-mitigation (12:45-12:55): throughput recovered ~85% of baseline, p95 latency back to normal
profiling-bot: collected heap snapshots and KV index stats; fragmentation hotspot appears to be with 256MB transient allocations from kernel workspace on small batches
maria: follow-ups: 1) short-term: keep throttle in place until we finish rollout of kv cache pinning and adjust small-batch kernel heuristics 2) mid-term: change kernel_selector to consider fragmentation (prefer kernels that use smaller working sets for small batches) 3) long-term: allocator compaction + per-tenant soft limits for small-batch flows
jasper: filed an action item: ENG-RUNTIME-402 — "investigate allocator compaction and kernel heuristics for small-batch workloads" linking logs and profiler dumps
ana: (reaction) :thumbsup: 
maria: thanks all — leaving throttle in place, will schedule a post-incident sync tomorrow 09:30 PT
